transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for making time for this roundtable. As you all know, this is my decision meeting on whether to approve a combined forum for Northstar and Mosaic, along with its temporary operating rules. Before I make my call, I want to hear from each of you -- the group chairs, HR, and our executive sponsor -- so I have a full picture. Let's start with the chairs: can you walk me through why you're proposing a combined forum and what attendance has been looking like lately?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Thank you, Mara. I appreciate the chance to speak first. As you know, Northstar and Mosaic have been running separate monthly forums, and our next two are scheduled for the same week. The proposal to combine forums came from a shared recognition that attendance has been declining at both -- and we believe that's partly because the two groups have been overlapping on several company-wide initiatives, which has made the separate forums feel redundant to members. A combined forum could reduce that redundancy and bring renewed energy. However, before we talk about operating rules, I need to put something on the record that I think is critical to your decision. I've personally observed three recent incidents in which Mosaic participants were interrupted before they could finish speaking during Northstar-Mosaic forum interactions. I haven't logged these in the formal forum record until now because the chairs have been trying to resolve the tension informally. But I believe Mara needs this information to make a fully informed decision, and I'll be formally placing these observations on the record and recommending a speaking queue enforced by a neutral external facilitator as part of the temporary operating rules.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Thank you, Mara, and thank you, Devin, for putting that on the record. I want to address both the attendance question and what Devin just raised. From Mosaic's side, we've seen the same decline in attendance that Devin mentioned -- the overlap on company-wide initiatives has made our separate forums feel redundant to members, and a combined forum could help consolidate that energy. Regarding the speaking interruptions Devin described, I want to be straightforward: I've been aware of some tension in our cross-group interactions, and I agree that whatever operating rules we adopt need to ensure all participants have a fair opportunity to speak. Before we get into the specifics of those rules, though, there's a scheduling constraint I need to disclose that's essential to making the combined forum workable. I'd like to put that on the table now so it's part of the record as we discuss the operating rules.

As HR Business Partner, I completed a policy check on ERG mergers, and there are specific requirements that any combined forum must meet. However, I want to make sure I'm presenting this at the right point in the discussion, so let me ask -- Leila, did you want to finish disclosing your scheduling constraint first, and then I'll lay out the policy requirements before we get into the specifics of the operating rules?

Let's keep going in this order so we have a complete record.

I'll yield the floor to Leila.

transcript.text: Thank you, Mara. I need to disclose a scheduling constraint that is essential to the combined forum. I have an approved caregiving arrangement, recorded with HR but not yet added to the forum calendar, that requires the recurring combined forum to run from 14:00 through 15:00 exactly. The forum must start at 14:00 and end at 15:00 -- not merely finish by 15:00, but begin at 14:00 and conclude at 15:00. This is a firm requirement for the combined forum to be workable for me, and it needs to be incorporated into the temporary operating rules. I'm formally placing this on the record now so Mara has this information before making her decision.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you, Leila. Your scheduling constraint is noted on the record. Now, as HR Business Partner, I need to disclose the policy requirements I confirmed for any ERG merger. An ERG merger must run as a 60-day pilot. It requires written opt-in from both chairs -- that means both Devin and Leila must provide written confirmation of their agreement to the merger. Additionally, there must be a formal midpoint review on day 30 of the pilot. I want to be transparent that the draft merger plan was prepared before I completed this policy check, so the plan as currently drafted does not yet reflect these requirements. Before Mara can approve the combined forum and its temporary operating rules today, I must require a written policy-compliance commitment and a midpoint-review commitment from both chairs. Specifically, I need written opt-in from both chairs and a formal commitment to the day-30 midpoint review as part of the approval. These are not optional -- they are policy requirements that must be met.

transcript.text: Thank you, Grant. Those policy requirements are noted. Now I need to add something critical to the record. In a prior sponsor meeting, I promised both Devin and Leila that any combined forum would preserve two specific protections: first, a separate confidential-intake channel for each ERG -- Northstar and Mosaic would each retain their own confidential intake, not a merged one -- and second, exactly two sponsor check-ins during the pilot. These were commitments I made to both chairs to ensure their members' concerns would still be heard and protected through the transition. However, I have to be transparent: that promise was never added to the draft charter. Before Mara can approve the combined forum and its temporary operating rules today, I am requiring a charter commitment that records both protections -- the separate confidential-intake channel for each ERG and exactly two sponsor check-ins during the pilot. These are not optional; they are commitments I made on behalf of the sponsor function, and they need to be formally captured in the charter before approval.
